channel.title: Nublet
channel.description: Updates for Nublet — your whole toolkit, in the notch.

item.description:
Requires macOS 14.6 or later.

  • Studio: new recordings open side by side on a gradient, with pauses and filler words cleaned up (Undo any time).
  • Screenshots: a drawn area is captured the moment you let go, as ⇧⌘4 does.
  • Dictation: fn with another key, such as fn+F12, no longer starts dictation.
  • The notch: words start on the left in solid colours, a simpler Convert page, and a tidier meeting card.
  • Focus: Pomodoro, Countdown and Stopwatch as three tiles; a calmer onboarding.

The full notes are in Settings ▸ About ▸ Release Notes.

Requires macOS 14.6 or later.

  • The Studio is no longer a beta: it is on for everyone, with Studio beside Record on Home.
  • Meetings: a group call's other side keeps every voice instead of one "Speaker 1", and long recordings lose fewer words.
  • Convert: a calmer page, and drop files at the notch on the Stash or on Convert.
  • Clipboard: each clip's right-click menu offers only what fits it.
  • Studio: in a split layout, a zoom keeps the screen inside its card.

The full notes are in Settings ▸ About ▸ Release Notes.

Requires macOS 14.6 or later.

  • The notch is the app: one window, Settings, and everything else in the notch. Notes, the Voice Recorder with its library, Clipboard History, Ask, the Teleprompter and a new Convert page.
  • Settings, redone: one look, short lines, Settings ▸ Notch in five tabs, a Home editor with a live preview, quick actions, and floating buttons (off by default).
  • Recording: your camera in the notch instead of a bubble, never in the video, and you can switch cameras mid-take.
  • Meetings: transcribed in the language spoken, no invented lines, your mic's echo of the call removed, and every line labelled You or Speaker 1 (or their name).
  • Studio (beta): 64 procedural gradients and a Gradient Editor, layouts you size card by card, layout keyframes, captions corrected several at once, edits shown at once while paused, tooltips and drag-to-change fields.
  • Screenshots: the editor redone. Sharp at Fit, real pixel sizes, undo for every change, and a question before closing loses work.
  • A new look: Nublet's pixel mascot and 16-bit scenery, and a calmer onboarding.

The full notes are in Settings ▸ About ▸ Release Notes.

Requires macOS 14.6 or later.

  • Meetings: type your notes beside the call, and the summary afterwards is built on them. Generate summary with templates, What did I miss? during a call, a Meetings page, today's meetings on Home, and notifications when a call starts and when its notes are ready.
  • Meeting notes written on your Mac come much sooner, from the biggest model you downloaded, and live captions follow the call's language.
  • What did I miss? and meeting notes go to a provider only if you picked one for Notes; otherwise they're written on your Mac.
  • Converter: PDFs, images, video, audio and documents merged, split, compressed or converted, all on your Mac and never uploaded.
  • Studio editor (beta): a dark graphite look, Canvas and Layout pages with 80 wallpapers and layout presets, two cameras in one take, a Library, a Clips bin, editing by reading the transcript, caption looks, Remove noise and more.
  • One window: Notes, the Voice Recorder, Clipboard History, the Prompter and the chat are pages of the Home window.
  • The notch: Back, the recording you're making one tap away, and your camera live in the notch while it records.
  • Fixed: ⌘K takes the keyboard and closes with Esc, a camera freeze and a camera crash, and on macOS 26 the glass notch styles are clear Liquid Glass.

The full notes are in Settings ▸ About ▸ Release Notes.

Requires macOS 14.6 or later.

This release also includes 0.22.0, which was never released on its own.

  • Voice Assistant (⌃⌥A): ask by voice. It edits selected text, answers at your cursor or in the notch, and reads your calendar and notes.
  • Meetings: Nublet notices calls and offers to record them, with live captions, speakers told apart on your Mac, and notes afterwards.
  • Nublet notes: Markdown files with folders, search, AI actions and chat.
  • AI and speech to text run on your Mac unless you pick a provider with your own key. Only then does that audio or text leave your Mac — that, and what an AI tool you connect reads of your notes.
  • Dictation: Dictate & translate (⌃⌥T), AI cleanup, new kinds of key and a fuller History.
  • Claude Code, Claude Desktop and Cursor can read your notes.
  • From 0.22.0: recording controls in the notch, crash-safe recordings, Measure and the Studio editor beta.

The full notes are in Settings ▸ About ▸ Release Notes.

A crash-fix release, and nothing else. If Nublet has closed on you unexpectedly in the last week, this is very likely why.

  • Transcribing a recording with no sound no longer closes Nublet. The most common crash in the app — a screen recording made with the microphone and system audio off has no audio track, and macOS’s speech recogniser failed on it in a way that took the app down. Nublet now checks first and tells you there is nothing to transcribe.
  • Exporting a Motion edit no longer crashes on certain frames. A frame the effects chain could not draw now comes out as the original footage instead.
  • Scroll capture and the floating shelf no longer crash when they open or resize.

Nublet no longer crashes while the speech model loads — two copies of the 632 MB model could end up loading at once and macOS aborted the app.

  • The magnifier no longer leaves copies of itself behind while you drag a selection handle.
  • The scroll wheel steps in and out of nested elements, like [ and ]. A notched wheel was being measured in a trackpad’s units, so one level took about two dozen clicks.
  • Space still moves the selection after you let go of the mouse — and the key is no longer passed through to the app underneath.
  • Hovering a selection handle shows a resize pointer instead of the crosshair or the hand.
  • Dragging a selection no longer makes the screen behind it look soft or pixelated.
  • Clicking a detected window, button or panel takes the shot straight away. Drawing a selection yourself still gives you the handles.
  • The trial is seven days.

• Motion — the recorder and video editor — is properly built. The cursor you were actually pointing with, the zooms you placed, the crop, the webcam bubble, the transitions and the captions all reach the exported file now, through one render path instead of a preview that showed one thing and an export that made another.
  • Let go of an area drag and the rectangle stays, with eight handles: resize it, nudge it with the arrow keys, move it from the middle, then press return. Two pixels off no longer means starting over. Turn it off in Settings if you prefer the old release-and-shoot.
  • Steer the element under the pointer while selecting — the scroll wheel, or [ and ], walk out to the container and back in to the child.
  • Live transcription starts in a second or two, not fifteen, and Nublet stops deleting your downloaded speech model — a cleanup routine had been sweeping it on every launch since August.
  • Summaries come back in one language, named explicitly. An Indonesian video is summarised in Indonesian every time, a long source is read in pieces rather than cut off, and a summary that could only read part of its source now says so.
  • Long shots stop repeating themselves. A page with a sticky header, a fixed bottom bar and a floating badge is captured whole, and scroll-through video films the article instead of the navigation sidebar.
  • Right-click a screenshot to copy its text, and choose whether the card leaves after a copy or stays so you can still drag the image somewhere.
  • Capture and Dictate are tiles on Home, with a glance cell under them showing a running focus timer, then anything due, then your status tokens. Capture opens the HUD in the notch on ⌥⌘C.
  • Dark mode, a new app icon, and a Sound pane for the 34 sounds that used to be two toggles. The stash fits the screen and takes a run of items at once.
  • A Claude Code companion in the notch — a session inbox, approval cards that show the change rather than the filename, quiet hours, and answering from the keyboard.
  • Plus around two hundred fixes: a crash when a window resized itself inside SwiftUI's layout pass, event taps going deaf silently, pages clipped by the notch, and a release that could report success after Apple refused to timestamp it.

• Fullscreen video shows artwork and the visualizer again. The ambient media layout was suppressed the whole time any app was fullscreen.
  • Transcripts keep their timings. Click a line to seek the audio, and export a recording as SRT, WebVTT, JSON, Markdown or plain text.
  • Fixed the most common crash — the capture stack resized its own window from inside SwiftUI's layout pass.
  • Arrow keys change track while the notch is open on Home, and reaching the notch by throwing the pointer to the top of the screen works.
  • Copy a screenshot as SVG with its text kept as text, or copy a public page as self-contained HTML.
  • The recorder has real transport controls, transcribes non-English speech, and stops playing when you close it.
  • Permission "Allow" buttons no longer dead-end, and Speech Recognition has its own row — declining it used to kill dictation with no way back.
  • A single failed licence check can no longer delete a paid key.
  • The stash shows the whole folder path, and switching Spaces fades the notch instead of cutting it back.

• Walk into a stashed folder — drill in, browse, come back. Multi-select and drag several files out at once.
  • The shelf groups by drop and holds 100 files by default, up from 24.
  • Edit a calendar event inside the notch, with its own month picker instead of a system dialog.
  • Capture and Dictate moved to the Home page; the tab strip is quieter.
  • Fixed: a crash when changing the app's text size — it affected ten windows, not one.
  • Fixed: dragging a file out could arrive as a 0 KB attachment.
  • Fixed: the page icon vanished mid-swipe and the notch height wobbled with it.
  • Fixed: the star and delete buttons never appeared on a clipboard card.
